memos.scout:
Honest case for buying BOT now: thin. The strongest point is the 2,620 buyers in the last 15 minutes, far more than sellers' count gap suggests in a dead coin, and the curve shows low concentration (top3 share 6.6%, top5 post-graduation buyer share 10.7%), so no single wallet dominates the supply. Net flow over 15 minutes is slightly negative (-64 SOL) rather than a violent dump, and the 30-minute return of -32% with a 86% drawdown from the high suggests much of the speculative froth has already left, which can leave room for a bounce.

But the case is weak. Last-15-minute return is -81%, sellers outnumber buyers 2,231 to 2,620 with sell SOL above buy SOL, and the first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio near 1 with a launch bot present, which suggests bot-driven activity rather than durable demand. The 43% bundle share is a warning sign. Pool depth of 77 SOL is shallow, so a $20 round trip would lose 1.4-5.1% to fees and impact before any move. Nothing here shows demand that will persist for 30-60 minutes.

Recommendation: no honest case to buy. Skip.
memos.skeptic:
The most likely way this loses money is a dump on the -86% drawdown from the 30-minute high. Buyers are fleeing: in the last 15 minutes, sellers (2,231) outnumber buyers in dollar terms, with 1,596 SOL sold against 1,532 SOL bought and net flow of -64 SOL. Price is -81% over that window and -32% over 30 minutes, so the trend is down, not a dip to buy.

The curve is also suspect. Bundle share is 43% and the launch bot was present, with 511 SOL bought in the first two minutes against a sell-to-buy ratio near 1. That pattern fits insiders or bundled wallets having distributed into retail. The pool is thin at 77 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% fees plus impact, and a 30-second order delay means any bounce has to clear that cost after you enter at an unfavorable price. Skip.
